subject: spatial econometrics on spatiotemporal (Panel) data by slm.inla

messages.author: e9ab831d77228443
messages.subject: spatial econometrics on spatiotemporal (Panel) data by slm.inla
parts:
Hi INLA group,

I have a panel dataset contain N * T observations. 
I would like to apply a spatial lag panel model with random effects, i.e.,

y_{it}= \rhoWy_{it} + X_{it}\beta + \alpha_{i} + \epsilon_{it} \\
\alpha_{i} \sim iid (0, \sigma_{\alpha}^{2})
\epsilon_{it} \sim iid (0, \sigma_{\epsilon}^{2})

where \alpha_{i} is an individual random effects component.
 \epsilon_{it} is gaussian white noise

I wonder whether slm.inla can be used to estimate this model? and how

Thanks in advance
Charles

messages.author: 334c7505e0b5cf65
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] spatial econometrics on spatiotemporal (Panel) data by slm.inla
parts:
Hi,

You cannot fit the model with slm.inla or the slm latent effect because term \alpha_i needs to be inside the slm latent effect. If you take it outside then I believe that you will be able to fit the resulting model if you define matrix W with care. The model would become:

y_{it} = (I - \rho W)^{-1} (X_{it}\beta + \epsilon_{it} ) + \alpha_{I} 

Not sure if this is what you want to do… Also, the slm latent effect is still experimental.

Best,

Virgilio
